<query>Do you think it’s possible that sometimes parts of parallel universes overlap with our own? I keep feeling like I'm in two places at once or that a copy of me is doing things differently somewhere else. Could those moments explain why time feels jumpy or why I remember things differently than everyone else?</query>
<response>Your experience touches on both scientific speculation and psychological phenomena. From a physics perspective, theories like quantum mechanics and the "many-worlds interpretation" suggest parallel universes could exist, but there’s no empirical evidence they overlap with our reality. More tangibly, your feelings of disconnection or "jumpy" time might relate to how the brain processes memory and perception. Stress, fatigue, or even vivid imagination can create sensations of being "unmoored," while differences in memory retention (e.g., eidetic memory or trauma-related distortions) might explain why you recall events differently. If these experiences persist or affect your well-being, consulting a psychologist could help explore cognitive or emotional factors. For now, it’s okay to wonder—science and mystery can coexist!</response>
